title: San Jose Clean Energy EcoHome Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps and Water Heaters
desc: What San Jose Clean Energy's EcoHome program pays in 2026: heat pump water heater $3,000, heat pump HVAC $1,500, insulation and panel add-ons. The battery rebate is closed.
h1: San Jose Clean Energy EcoHome Rebates
lead: San Jose Clean Energy's EcoHome program pays $3,000 for a heat pump water heater and $1,500 for a heat pump HVAC system, with add-ons for insulation and electrical work. The rebate must be approved before you install, and the old battery rebate is closed.
cards_intro: We read San Jose Clean Energy's pages on October 1, 2026. Higher amounts apply in environmental justice communities. Each card names the fact with the date and a source link.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Includes a $500 bonus for applications from September 1 to October 31, 2026. Must replace a gas appliance, and the rebate must be approved before install.

cards.title: Heat pump HVAC
cards.note: Must replace a gas appliance, with rebate approved before install.

cards.title: Attic insulation add-on
cards.note: Up to $1,000 in EJ communities. Must be paired with a heat pump HVAC rebate.

cards.title: Panel and circuit add-ons
cards.note: EJ communities: panel up to $2,000, circuits $750 each. Requires a heat pump HVAC or water heater.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: $125 per kWh up to $3,250 for applications submitted before July 1. Closed to new applications.

sections: San Jose Clean Energy buys and sells clean electricity for San Jose residents, while PG&E still delivers it. A San Jose address usually means SJCE, but check your bill. SJCE's rebates apply to SJCE customers only. Oakland, Berkeley and Fremont use a different clean energy provider and are not covered here.

The most common mistake is buying before the rebate is approved. SJCE asks for approval before installation, so get the rebate reserved, then book the work. Ask any contractor how they handle the reservation before you sign. The rebate also requires that the new equipment replace a gas appliance, so it does not cover electric-to-electric swaps.

A San Jose house outside an environmental justice community replaces a gas water heater and a gas furnace. The heat pump water heater earns $3,000, including the $500 bonus while it lasts, and the heat pump HVAC earns $1,500, so $4,500 together. Add a $1,000 panel upgrade and 1,000 square feet of attic insulation at $0.75, which is $700 under the cap, and the full project reaches $6,200. In an environmental justice community the same job earns more on every line. These sums use SJCE's published amounts, and each item has its own conditions.

Insulation, panel and circuit add-ons are only available with a heat pump HVAC or water heater rebate. A heat pump water heater at $3,000 plus a $1,000 panel upgrade is $4,000. Add attic insulation, which needs a heat pump HVAC rebate, and a full house project can reach several thousand dollars more. Each add-on has its own rules, so read the page for the item before you sign a contract.

The battery rebate closed to new applications for anything submitted on or after July 1. We found no SJCE rebate for rooftop solar. State and federal money adds little in 2026. TECH Clean California lists its single-family funds as reserved, the federal home electrification rebates are on hold, and the federal 25C and 25D credits ended after December 31, 2025.
claim_heading: How to claim an EcoHome rebate
claim_steps: Confirm your account is with San Jose Clean Energy.
Choose the equipment and a contractor, then apply to reserve the rebate.
Wait for approval before any installation begins.
Install the equipment to replace a gas appliance.
Submit your final documents and wait for payment.

faq: How much does San Jose Clean Energy pay for a heat pump water heater?
$3,000, or $4,000 in environmental justice communities, with a $500 bonus for applications from September 1 to October 31, 2026.
Can I install first and apply later?
No. SJCE asks that the rebate be approved before installation.
Is the battery rebate still open?
No. It closed to new applications.
Does it cover replacing an electric appliance?
No. The new equipment must replace a gas appliance.
Can I get the insulation add-on alone?
No. It must be paired with a heat pump HVAC rebate.
